function: DDPG agent allocates transmit power and resource-block priority to vehicles on V2I and ground-to-air links, then an LLM transfers RBs and updates powers for failed tasks (pp. 9-11).
system: 5 UAVs (50-100 m altitude), 50 vehicles, one ground BS; 2.4 GHz, 10 MHz in 180 kHz resource blocks; antenna gains only, no array; no RIS (pp. 4, 13).
method: DDPG actor-critic reinforcement learning (MLP actor and critic, replay buffer) plus pretrained Qwen3-235B-A22B LLM used with few-shot in-context prompting and KV caching (pp. 9-11, 13).
data_channel: Simulated custom channel: V2I path loss 128.1+37.6log10(d/1000), shadowing, Rayleigh fading; air-ground LoS-probability path loss from [37] with K-factor fading; 300 m x 300 m road scene (pp. 3-5).
test_conditions: One scenario with 50 vehicles and 5 UAVs; loads of 30 to 50 Mb per slot swept; training and test conditions are not described separately (pp. 13-15).
baselines: Resource scheduling: standalone DDPG without LLM (ablation); trajectory: CVX, LVM, MADQN; offloading: LP versus MADDPG; Full-MADRL combination; no non-learned resource-allocation baseline (p. 13).
metrics: Average delay, weighted normalized energy, task success rate, total objective (36a), and coverage metric Rt for trajectories (pp. 14-15).
complexity: Order of complexity per decision slot, Eq. (61): O(Ltraj U (K^3.5+MK) + Lloop[(Sdyn+Sout)Pact+2M^3.5]); LLM activates about 22 billion parameters (p. 13).
openness: Source code and LLM prompt released at https://github.com/qiongwu86/Joint-Optimization-of-Trajectory-Control-RA-and-Task-Offloading-for-Multi-UAV-Assisted-IoV (p. 2).
q1_support: p. 4: "= 128.1 + 37.6 × log10". The V2I path loss is a custom formula with shadowing and Rayleigh fading, and the air-ground model comes from [37] (p. 5), with no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data, so not met.
q2_support: p. 14: "Fig. 7 shows the average system task completion time under" different total loads (30 to 50 Mb, Table I). This is a load sweep, and the paper never says the DDPG is trained in one condition and tested in another, so not met.
q3_support: p. 13: "DDPG baseline (ablation study)". The only resource-allocation baseline is the proposed method without the LLM; MADQN, LVM and MADDPG replace the trajectory and offloading modules, and no non-learned resource-scheduling baseline is given, so not met.
q4_support: p. 13: "the total computational complexity per decision slot" is given in Eq. (61) as an order of complexity covering the trajectory SOCP, the DRL and LLM inference and the LP.
q5_support: p. 2: "The source code and LLM prompt have been released at" a GitHub link given in footnote 1.
notes: Kept under the aerial-link rule: the learned part is the DDPG agent, with the LLM, that controls transmit power and resource blocks on V2I and ground-to-air links (pp. 9-11), which is area 6. The UAV trajectory (SOCP, pp. 7-9) and offloading ratios (LP, pp. 11-12) are not learned and sit above the physical layer. The LLM is pretrained and used by prompting, with no training described. DDPG training details are not given. The V2I formula resembles a 3GPP macro formula, but the paper does not cite 3GPP.
